name: Numerical Estimation/Slider

tier.label: Apply — Using Information in New Contexts

summary: Move a slider along a scale or type a number to estimate a value. Proximity to the correct value determines partial credit.

aiGenerability.notes: AI generates numerical estimation questions and defines correct value plus acceptable range/margin of error. Works for any quantifiable fact: dates, distances, populations, measurements.

prompt.description: Question asking for a numerical estimate. Must be clear about units and context.

correctValue.description: The correct answer (numeric, no units in the field).

minValue.description: Minimum value for the slider range.

maxValue.description: Maximum value for the slider range.

unit.description: Unit of measurement (e.g., 'years', 'kilometers', 'millions', '%'). Displayed in the UI.

acceptableRange.description: Margin of error (±) for full credit. Example: acceptableRange = 10 means ±10 from correctValue earns full points.

explanation.description: Explanation of the correct answer and its context.

precision.description: Number of decimal places to round to (0 for integers, 2 for decimals). Default: 0.

ux.mobileNotes: Slider thumb is 48×48px min. Current value displays above or inside the thumb as learner drags. Range min/max labels at slider ends. Optional numeric input field below slider for precise entry.

ageAdaptations.8-10: Smaller numerical ranges (1–100). Wide acceptable range (±20–30). Visual number line with marked increments (0, 25, 50, 75, 100). Explanation is simple and concrete.
ageAdaptations.11-13: Moderate ranges (1–2000). Standard acceptable range (±10–15). Slider shows marks every 250 or 500 units. Explanation includes context or reference points.
ageAdaptations.14-16: Large, precise ranges (1–10000+). Tight acceptable range (±5–10). Fine-grained slider with optional direct numeric input field. Explanation includes calculations, derived data, or cross-referenced facts.
